Byte-exact roundtrip (truth = real git 2.55): reading a git-written .git/index and writing it back reproduces the exact original bytes (assert_eq! over fs::read) for each of:
- diverse worktree: nested dir, chmod +x file, symlink, UTF-8 name (中文文件.txt), and a 4095-byte deep path;
- committed index carrying git's full cache-tree TREE extension;
- conflicted index from `git merge` (stage 1/2/3 entries, plus REUC);
- assume-valid entry (`git update-index --assume-unchanged`);
- injected unknown extension (signature ZZzz);
- TREE + REUC ordering.
`git ls-files --stage` is unchanged before/after the rewrite, `git status --porcelain` stays empty, and `git update-index --refresh` / `git add` / `git fsck --no-progress` all succeed on the rewritten index. Parsed tree_oid equals `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`.

Negative cases: flipped trailer byte -> Error::Corrupt; version field set to 3 -> Error::Unsupported; truncated to 0/4/12/31 bytes -> Err(Corrupt) with no panic; missing .git/index -> empty Index (version 0); empty-index write (32 bytes) is readable by real git with empty `git ls-files --stage`. Name-length boundaries 4094/4095/4096 roundtrip.

Format facts that drove the implementation: long names (>=0xFFF) store flags low12 = 0xFFF and do NOT write an extra NUL (the mandatory 1..8 padding NULs terminate it; read finds the first NUL). Real git's TREE extension is a cache-tree of shape `name\0` + "<entry_count> <subtree_nr>\n" + oid(20), recursive, commonly far larger than 20 bytes, so its raw bytes are preserved verbatim in Index::extensions to guarantee byte equality while the root oid is parsed into Index::tree_oid. When tree_oid is set but no raw TREE data exists (programmatically built index), a 20-byte TREE extension is generated; git 2.55 reads that safely. Writes are atomic: .git/index.lock + rename.
